title: Book 10 opens: still on holy tent furnishings; word clear but not enough
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK TEN. Concerning the same things still, and concerning the things in the holy tent. Is the word clear to you then, O Palladius, and sufficient, which we have made upon the holy tent and the things in it?
notes_covered: Cyril asks if prior word suffices
translator_notes: §1 ends into Palladius reply in §2; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Pitch tent on new-moon first month; Moses builds Church-type; Jesus with Moses vs Amalek
english: Palladius: Clear indeed very well, yet sufficient least of all.

Cyril: Do you wish then that we most eagerly cross again unto that which seems to have been left behind in the narrations upon it? For you think somehow, according to what is likely, that the clarifying word must also be brought alongside, in what manner it has been raised for us, and when and how the righteous-ordinances and laws in it have been composed, and inauguration and sanctification and judgment.
Palladius: Speak then again the things upon each; for you think uprightly.

Cyril: So then I will speak. And you in turn be forgiving, having thought through the complete difficulty of the contemplations, and if somewhere I should chance to say something of the things that have missed exactness and have wandered out from the needed word, reshape and readjust. For I will make you a fellow-taker and helper of my own words.
Palladius: Go trusting God.

Cyril: So then when the works of the holy tent had been thoroughly completed, and indeed also each of the things in it wisely and artfully finished toward the beauty shown on the mountain, the Lord spoke toward Moses, saying, ‘On day one of the month the first, at new-moon, you will set up the tent of the testimony.’ And after other things again: ‘And it came to be,’ he says, ‘in the month the first, in the second year of their going out from Egypt, at new-moon, the tent was stood, and Moses set up the tent.’ So then the ancient tent of the Church thought in Christ has been raised according to what seemed good to God, showing the types very well upon itself. And let us busy ourselves, if it seems good, with the causes of its having been raised rather through Moses, Jesus the son of Nun being silent for the present, though always standing beside all-excellent Moses, and leaping up together upon the mountain Sinai, and also making war and leading out against Amalek through Moses’ voice. For he said somewhere toward him, ‘Choose for yourself strong men, and going out draw up against Amalek tomorrow.’ And he drew up, and he has conquered. What then is the word of this—is it not worthy to examine?
Palladius: Very much so.

Cyril: So then if someone should choose to exact the word of the mystery upon each of the things done as far as possible, marveling he will say, ‘O depth of wealth and wisdom and knowledge of God!’ For observe how subtle and necessary is the mind upon each: for when all-divine Moses runs up unto the mountain, Jesus goes up together; for the Father is not otherwise approachable, except through Son. For it is also true, if it should be said: ‘No one comes toward the Father, except through me.’ In Christ therefore also for the saints themselves is the approach; and no one would be able, as unto a mountain, to leap up unto some high and surpassing contemplation, nor would anyone, I think, come near God, according to manner clearly
notes_covered: Jesus of Nun with Moses / Amalek
translator_notes: Ends mid-word/phrase into §3 συναφείας; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Emmanuel makes rough ways passable; Moses’ pedagogy builds Church; one saving day
english: Cyril: …of joining, of the way of life in spirit and sanctification, unless Emmanuel also is present with him, and sets the things unreachable for humans as passable and horse-ridden. And this, I think, is what has been said through Isaiah’s voice, ‘Every ravine will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be lowered, and all the crooked will be unto a straight, and the rough unto smooth roads.’ For in Christ for us also the steep are smooth, and the rough is passable; and bare and level are the hard-to-travel. For also, as the prophet himself says somewhere again, ‘A road of pious ones. It has become straight, and prepared is the road of the pious.’ So then necessarily Jesus goes up together with all-divine Moses. For the Father is approachable, as I said, through Son, and he himself is the mediator, joining us through himself, and carrying us up into the heights beyond nature. And he had drawn up with chosen men, and was conquering Amalek. For Christ, having chosen the saints, of whom the all-divine disciples have become firstfruit, has conquered the ruler of this age; and Moses was the one commanding; for the Son has come to be under law, though existing as lawgiver as God. And the time of the battle-array was not being practiced according to that very day on which Moses’ words came to be, but unto the tomorrow—that is, unto a putting-off of another time. For the law foretold the things that would be, and has a bright narration of the Savior’s achievements, if it should be thought spiritually. In this way then, as I myself somehow think, Moses also raised the holy tent. For the pedagogy through law unto the constitution of the Church is not unhelpful. For it pedagogues unto Christ, who is the head of the Church, and the whole constitution, pillar and foundation of the truth, according to what has been written. And indeed Christ has addressed Jews: ‘If you were believing Moses, you would also believe me; for concerning me that one wrote.’ So then Moses also builds—that is, the pedagogy through law—the Church of Christ, still showing beforehand as in shadows the mystery upon it. And Moses’ person sometimes presents the law through him, according at least to what has been uprightly said in Gospel parables, ‘They have Moses and the prophets.’
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: And what again would the needing on day one wish to signify, and indeed also the new-moon of the month the first, and the needing for the holy tent to be pegged in the second year—come then let us say, tracking the true, and what seems to hold most excellently for those who will meet it. For day the one shows beforehand for us the much-prayed and saving time, according to which the Only-begotten having become human acquired those upon the earth for God and Father by the death of his own flesh. And one is the time of this of all; for having died once, he no longer dies; death will no longer lord over him, according to the Scriptures; for we will not still expect the Son to die for us ourselves and for the spirits in Hades, nor yet
translator_notes: Continues §2 mid-cut συναφείας; ends mid into §4 firstfruit a second time.

title: One acceptable day; apostles build Gentile Church; Christ many-formed in believers
english: Cyril: …to become firstfruit of those who have fallen asleep a second time. For if death will not be, how would resurrection also come to be? So then it is not to speak falsely when saying that one is the time of this, as I said just now, and day one, of which the prophet also made mention saying as from God’s person, ‘In an acceptable time I heard you, and in a day of salvation I helped you.’ And all-divine Paul also writes, ‘Behold now an acceptable time, behold now a day of salvation,’ according to which Christ lived again from dead ones, having dissolved the unsmiling power of death, when also he was setting the holy apostles as somehow builders and spiritual craftsmen of the Church from nations, saying, ‘Going, disciple all the nations, baptizing them unto the name of the Father and of the Son and of the holy Spirit, teaching them to keep all things, as many as I commanded you; and behold I am with you all the days until the completion of the age.’ For do you not say that this is the constitution of the Church?
Palladius: What then do you say?

Cyril: The faith handed over through the holy mystagogues, and the way of life proclaimed—I mean the one in Christ—and the union toward God through holy baptism, through participation of the holy Spirit. For thus Paul was addressing us saying, ‘And you as living stones are being built up a spiritual house, unto a holy temple, unto a dwelling of God in Spirit.’ For long ago Christ was being pre-formed as in differing vessels in the holy tent—as golden censer, as ark, as lampstand, and indeed also as table, and the things in it; and each, I think, of those who have believed, according at least to the present time, is named house and temple of God, having Christ dwelling within. For he dwells in our hearts through the faith, as has been written, existing one and the same according to nature, even if he should be thought with flesh. ‘For one God the Father, from whom are all things, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things,’ having upon himself the as-it-were many-formed through the differing properties of the godhead, and being thought differently. For he is in us as Word of God, and wisdom, and light, and life, and the living bread also from heaven.
Palladius: I have understood what you say.

Cyril: So then the time of the becoming-human for us, and the thrice-longed day of the resurrection from dead ones, was being typed beforehand long ago through God’s saying, On day one you will set up the tent. And the, And at new-moon of the month the first, one would see as usefully and necessarily brought alongside, O Palladius. For just as beginning of a month is the first of days in it—that is, the new-moon—so also somehow a beginning of a new age, and a first-entrance of newness of times, is the time of the sojourn. ‘For a new creation in Christ; the ancient things have passed.’ And as it were the age after this shines up for us, now still seen as in hopes, but then also about to be present
translator_notes: Ends mid-sentence into §5 truly when Christ shines again.

title: Spring new-moon = Gentile Church; second year after law; unshaken tents of Jerusalem
english: Cyril: …truly, when Christ should shine upon us again with the holy angels in the glory of the Father, about to take alongside himself those who have chosen to walk in newness of life, and who have enriched in endurance the most conspicuous beauty of the Gospel way of life, and bringing them into the glory and kingdom long expected. And that a new creation and as it were a new sprout of times and matters belongs to those in Christ, the riddle of the first month would show very well, according to which soft and newly-appearing grasses are on earth, and sprouting-again of plants, and the many-formed beauty of flowers in meadows is shown, of spring laughing fragrance; for somehow in such a time Christ has called the Church from nations, saying thus, ‘Rise, come, my neighbor, my fair one, my dove, because behold the winter has gone away, the rain has gone away, it has traveled in it; the flowers have been seen on the earth; time of cutting has arrived.’ For human nature has sprouted again, as some plant, having been withered by death, both through the transgression in Adam and through the sin that tyrannized over all of us. And I hear Christ saying also through one of the holy prophets, ‘I myself who speak am present, as an hour upon the mountains.’ For what spring works in mountains and thickets, crowning the plants with new sprout, this also our Savior’s presence has fulfilled upon us, having come to be according to times, as in a second year, and not at least in the first time, according to which the law was, and the chorus of the prophets, and according to which death was ruling. For it has reigned from Adam and until Moses. So then as in a second year—that is, as in a time after the first, according to which the law was—the Church from nations has shone up, having Christ as inmate, the end of the prophets and of the law. Does the word seem to you to shoot through toward the straight and true?
Palladius: Altogether so.

Cyril: And I myself think that the more true tent has been announced beforehand for us through Isaiah’s voice, saying as toward each of those called in faith unto righteousness, ‘Your eyes will see Jerusalem, rich cities, tents which will not be shaken, nor will the pegs of its tent be moved; nor will its ropes be torn apart unto the age-long time.’ For the Church is God’s city, of which also all-divine David made mention saying, ‘Glorious things have been spoken concerning you, the city of God.’ For this is rich, and adorned with the gifts from above and from heaven, and having an unbreakable standing in firmness, a seating and remaining. ‘For gates of Hades will not overpower it,’ according to the Savior’s voice.
Palladius: You think most uprightly and fittingly.
Cyril: And when the tent has been raised, that it is fitting for the things in it to lie in order, and not poured-out and carelessly, the Master God of all teaches saying:
notes_covered: Song 2:10-12 spring call to Gentile Church
translator_notes: Ends at God’s command quote opening §6.

title: Place vessels; veil of four pillars; Holies / Holies of holies; laver between
english: Cyril: ‘And you will set the ark of the testimony, and you will cover the ark with the veil. And you will bring in the table, and you will set forth its setting-forth. And you will bring in the lampstand, and you will set on its lamps. And you will set the golden altar, unto incense opposite the ark. And you will set a covering of veil upon the door of the tent of the testimony, and you will set the altar of the fruit-offerings beside the doors of the tent of the testimony. And you will put around the tent, and you will put around all its things in a circle.’ But it is possible in these to see the holy vessels brought into the holy tent; yet not still also clearly the place fitting and allotted to each. Do you wish then that from the commands upon the tent we gather a subtle and exact knowledge of such things?
Palladius: As most pleasantly.

Cyril: So then God said toward holy Moses: ‘And you will make a veil from hyacinth and purple, and spun scarlet, and twined linen; a woven work you will make it Cherubim. And you will set it upon four undecaying pillars gilded with gold. And their capitals gold, and their bases four silver. And you will set the veil upon the pillars, and you will bring in there inward of the veil the ark of the testimony. And the veil will divide for you between the Holy, and between the Holy of holies. You will cover with the veil the ark of the testimony in the Holy of holies. And you will set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table upon the part of the tent toward south. And you will set the table upon the part of the tent toward north. And you will make a curtain for the door of the tent from hyacinth and purple, and spun scarlet, and spun linen, a work of an embroiderer. And you will make for the veil five pillars, and you will gild them with gold; and their capitals gold, and you will cast for them five bronze bases.’ And these things concerning these. And concerning the laver he somehow says thus: ‘Make a bronze laver, and a base for it bronze so as to wash, and you will set it between the tent of the testimony, and between the altar.’ Is the word upon each clear to you?
Palladius: Not at all; for I have been at a loss, know; and what the matter is, I am not able to say.

Cyril: So then upon each of the sayings set forth, having seized what finishes unto the contemplation upon them, I will make the narration clear and most distinct, as I am able. For the holy tent has been raised, O Palladius, according to the desert, as in a double placing and form. And one was the innermost; and its name, the Holies of holies. And as somehow a first-entrance and around it the first, the so-called Holies. And into the innermost tent the ark was set away, having upon four golden pillars a hanging made artfully from hyacinth and purple, and spun scarlet, and twined linen. Having
notes_covered: Exod 30 laver between tent and altar
translator_notes: Ends mid-sentence Εἰρηκότες into §7; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Veil = Christ’s flesh; four pillars = evangelists; Word hidden until resurrection
english: Cyril: …spoken already, and, as I myself somehow think, sufficiently the things upon the linen and the purple, and the spun scarlet, and indeed also hyacinth, we will push aside the same-speaking; yet that at least we will say for the present: The veil upon four golden pillars, whose bases are silver, was then hinting the mystery of Christ. For what? Did not wise Paul also name for us Christ’s body a veil, saying thus, ‘Which he inaugurated for us a fresh and living way through the veil, that is, of his flesh’?
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: Observe then as in shadows and riddles, that being God and from God Father according to nature the Word has come to be as in a golden and undecaying ark, the temple from Virgin; for undecaying and honored is Christ’s body; and he was all but also being hidden as in an order of a veil, having taken the flesh; and we say the Word from God is hidden, not as having been limited in a small body; for everywhere and in all things is the Son; but by escaping notice economically, and enduring the time of the showing-forth. And the time of showing-forth unto all is the living-again from dead ones. For before the honored cross, he was ordering the holy disciples that they not make him apparent. For it has been written thus. And after at least living again having suffered the death, ‘Going,’ he says, ‘disciple all the nations, baptizing them unto the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the holy Spirit.’ So then the veil was hanging upon the pillars, covering within the ark, and it would be a type of Christ, being raised high by the proclamations of the holy evangelists, and being seen in glory of godhead by those in the holy tent—that is, the Church. And four are the pillars, golden and silver-around; and equal in number to them are the evangelists, bright and honored. So then the ark was lying, and from above downward the veil was extending, the one from linen and purple and the others, and it was making it not visible. And from above the veil and of the Cherubim unto right and left, God was naming, showing that he is also beyond every creation; and also all the uppermost of the rational ones—that is, the Seraphim—sit under the divine and ineffable glory, and escorting the Son himself, even if he has become flesh, and as somehow in a lowering of the equality toward the Father, according as he has been born human. Therefore also he himself was saying: ‘My Father is greater than I.’ And being equal according to nature to the one who has begotten, he says the coming-to-be in lesser things through only the human. On account of this also in the holy tent, in a circle of the veil, the Cherubim, and they themselves escorting the Son as God. And indeed also from above the veil itself, which was unto a type of Christ, God is thought. ‘And I will be known,’ he says, ‘from there, and I will speak to you.’ For beyond every creation is the Father, and of Emmanuel himself, not according as he is thought and is God; for he is equal according to all things to God; but as far as
translator_notes: Continues §6 Εἰρηκότες; ends mid into §8 slave-form measure.

title: Golden altar fragrance; lampstand south Jews / table north Gentiles
english: Cyril: …he has come unto a slave’s form, and unto a measure of humanity.
Palladius: How subtle the word and deep.
Cyril: Yet it comes not away from the aim.
Palladius: I agree.

Cyril: And with the ark holding thus, ‘And you will set,’ he says, ‘the golden altar unto incense opposite the ark.’ And that Christ is the golden altar, I think has been said sufficiently for us. Yet it has been set opposite the ark, upon which is the veil, and in a circle the Seraphim, and higher God, as somehow receiving the incomparable fragrance of Emmanuel. For he did not do sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth, as has been written; therefore also he himself was saying, ‘The Father loves the Son.’ And we ourselves also are acceptable to God, fragrant with Christ’s ointment. And Paul will also confirm writing: ‘And to God thanks who always triumphs us in the Christ, and who manifests the smell of his knowledge through us, because we are Christ’s fragrance to God.’
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: Let us think then exactly, casting the eye into the things written, that the ark has been seated in the flank of the holy tent toward southwest and west; and opposite it the golden altar, in the place toward ray. For dawn and setting have been filled with the Christ, and north and south. And indeed a place for the lampstand, the southern things of the tent; and for the table, the things toward north. And that through both the Christ is signified, a long word has already shown beforehand for us; for that Christ is light, the lampstand makes clear; and that life and living bread, the table and the things in it. Yet think that, and observe the mystery: for most southern is the country of the Jews, and more northern again that of the nations. So then from the placing of both—I mean of the lampstand and of the table—it will somehow remain for those who wish to think very well, that to the Jews Christ shone light, and among them he was proclaiming, ‘I am the light.’ For he has been sent unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel. And, ‘Theirs are the promises,’ according to the Scriptures. And since they did not accept the light of the truth, he has become for the nations life and bread from heaven; and not apart from light the nations; and this also you would learn, the light of the lampstand extending also unto the northern things of the tent. And with the holy tent being most narrow, nothing unlikely that the lampstand seems all but also to have been set beside the table, even if it should have the southern place. And the type also shows for us otherwise, that when divine light shines out those worthy would be able to share Christ, as living and true bread. And the nations have become joint-body and joint-sharers of Christ. And all-divine Paul writes again: And joint-body and joint-sharers have
notes_covered: lampstand south = Jews light; table north = Gentiles bread
translator_notes: Ends mid γέγονε into §9; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Five door pillars = fifth-age teachers; law altar at entrance; baptism laver mid-court
english: Cyril: …become the nations of light, clearly of the intelligible, being filled up additionally ‘while day is shining through, and Phosphoros rising according to mind,’ for one of the Savior’s disciples has said. And with placing and construction of the things in the Holies of holies holding thus, he has ordered a curtain, or veil, to come to be from hyacinth and purple, and spun scarlet, and twined linen; and this he was saying must necessarily be stretched around the entrances of the tent, being hung upon five golden pillars, whose bases are bronze. And he names curtain the hanging-around of the door, on account, I think, of being drawn back with fine rings when the entrance is pierced; and again being drawn against and widened of the doors, to hide the Holies. And five are the pillars, golden and bronze-around, typing beforehand the teachers and leaders of the Churches as in a fifth time, according to which Christ’s presence came to be; who, cutting-straight the word of the truth, are honored as gold, and well-sounding thus as bronze. ‘For unto all the earth their sound has gone out, and unto the ends of the inhabited world their words’; who also through artful and God-breathed mystagogy widen as it were the entrances for those wishing to run into the Holies of holies. So then the Holies of holies—that is, the more inward tent—was being covered with the veil. And at once the first tent also had been fixed beside and fitted to the second, having the altar of the fruit-offerings, in which every approach through bloods was being finished, and cakes and frankincenses, and every sacrifice and drink-offering, and indeed beside the altar also the bronze laver. And a place again for the altar beside the doors of the tent—clear that of the more outward; and for the laver, the most middle of the tent.
Palladius: And what again would the careful-watching be thought?

Cyril: Exact, O Palladius, is the holy Letter, and altogether nothing random in it. For see how the riddle has shown for us the law pedagoguing unto Christ. For the altar of the worship according to law has been set beside the very entrances unto the Holies of holies. For the law carries us off only barely unto beginnings of the mysteries of Christ, and somehow beside the first entrances of exact knowledge upon him; and it brings in in no way unto the Holies of holies—that is, unto the more inward tent, in which Christ is many-formed, as Word of God, as light, as living bread, as smell of fragrance to God and Father. For would you not say that elements and beginnings of the oracles of God were the pre-practice of the worship according to law?
Palladius: True.
Cyril: And that the law has perfected nothing, ‘For impossible for blood of bulls and goats to take away
notes_covered: five pillars = teachers of fifth age / Church leaders
law altar at doors = pedagogy only to beginnings
translator_notes: Ends mid ἁμαρτίας into §10; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Laver = baptism; outer veil hides law; Paul on two tents / two covenants
english: Cyril: …sins,’ you would learn at once, and very without toil, having also thought through the need of the laver. For it was lying in the middle of the first tent bright and conspicuous, washing beforehand with water those running into the Holies of holies. For the law upon this had been set for the priests. So then also the seeming fullness in law is incomplete, hinting the cleansing through holy baptism, which washes out the holy race—I mean that of those justified in faith—to whom also the all-divine disciple has addressed saying, ‘But you a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people unto acquisition, that you may announce the excellences of the one who called us from darkness unto his marvelous light.’ And one must know that also upon the door of the outer tent a veil had been stretched around, so that the Holies might not be bare and apparent to those from outside—that is, the first tent, in which is the altar in law—the type again making clear, I think, that not even the law itself is apparent to those who happen by. For it has a covering, the letter, and has somehow been covered and veiled with the unclarity as in shadows.
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: So then in the first tent laver was lying and altar; and in the second and innermost, the ark and the lampstand; and indeed also the golden censer, upon which the fine incense, and table and breads. And all-divine Paul also makes mention of a golden jar having the manna. And indeed he also names for us Aaron’s rod, which he says has also been set away in the Holies of holies, as being well-versed in the holy Letters, and having known that especially the things oracled according to times, and ordered to blessed Moses from God. And he knows also table and lampstand being in the first tent. And he writes thus concerning the two covenants, ‘In saying new, he has made the first old. And what is being made old and aging is near disappearance. So then the first also had righteous-ordinances of worship, and the worldly holy; for a tent was constructed the first, in which both the lampstand and the table, and the setting-forth of the breads, which is called holy. And after the second veil a tent, the one called Holies of holies, having a golden censer, and the ark of the covenant covered round from everywhere with gold, in which a golden jar having the manna, and Aaron’s rod that sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant. And above it Cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy-seat,’ concerning which it is not now to speak part by part.
Palladius: So then if someone should choose to be fond of seeking, and should say the causes of the whole construction must be spoken, what word would come to be from us?
Cyril: That, O Palladius, some things before the construction of the holy tent, and some after this, he has ordered to come to be. For in the Exodus even
translator_notes: Ends mid-sentence into §11 Exodus construction order.

title: Before tent patterns: golden jar/manna = Word; Aaron’s rod after; Paul orders types
english: Cyril: …before the patterns concerning the holy tent were seen at all, and the commands upon it came to be, he has oracled the word upon the golden jar, knowing what would be. And after at least the pitching of the whole tent, in the Numbers we will find Aaron’s rod brought into the Holies of holies. And in the Leviticus God was legislating further concerning both lampstand, and indeed also table, the one in the first tent. And being law-learned, all-wise Paul passes by altogether nothing of the things that have come to be, and makes mention of first and middle and last things.
Palladius: You have spoken most excellently. Speak then each clearly and distinctly; for deep somehow altogether is the word upon them.

Cyril: Yes, you say uprightly. For the matter holds thus according to truth. And I will make of the narrations also the jar a beginning. For God was sending down, as rain, the manna to those from Israel according to the desert; for this was food and bread for them from above and from heaven. But that the thing done was not only as far as the sense-perceptible; for it also carries up as through type and shadow unto the needing to think, that according to times the Word from above for us and from Father will be present, as bread from heaven, as also the divine David hints for us saying: ‘Bread of heaven he gave them; bread of angels human ate.’ And we do not somehow say that the sense-perceptible manna is the bread from heaven and of angels. For the spirit is nourished spiritually, and body again according to its own nature—that is, bodily. And food of angels and bread fitting heavens and the spirits above is the Word from God Father. So then the manna was making clear Christ. And the type has nothing beneficial, unless the truth has been received. For this is a shadow of that, having come to be not through itself properly, but in order that it may paint something of the better things upon itself. On account of this Christ was making a wise rebuke to the crowds of Jews, because they marvel not rather at him as truth, but at Moses, the servant of the types. For he said thus, ‘Amen, amen I say to you, Moses has given you the manna; for the bread of God is the one having come down from the heaven, and giving life to the world. I am the living bread.’ So then setting the manna as an image of the Word having come down from above and from heaven, God has oracled the things upon the jar. And it has been written thus: ‘And Moses said: This is the saying which the Lord arranged, Fill the gomer of the manna, unto a storehouse unto your generations, that they may see the bread which you ate in the desert, as the Lord led you out from land of Egypt. And Moses said toward Aaron: Take one golden jar, and cast into it the gomer of the manna full, and you will set it away opposite God, unto keeping unto your generations, in which manner the Lord arranged for Moses. And Aaron set it away opposite the testimony, unto keeping.’ For just as we were saying that the ark having the divine word was hinting Emmanuel—for he was Word of God as in
translator_notes: Continues §10 mid-cut; ends mid into §12 holy temple from Virgin.

title: Golden jar fullness = deity bodily; jar before Father; Korah; twelve rods begin
english: Cyril: …holy temple, the one from Virgin I mean; in the same manner also the golden jar for us, travailing the sense-perceptible manna, shows the Word from above and life-making, clear that the one from Father, as in a holy and unstained body. And the jar also is filled full of the manna. ‘For in him all the fullness of the godhead has dwelt bodily,’ according at least to blessed Paul’s voice. ‘And not from measure does he give the Spirit.’ For Christ is all-perfect. And the jar was set away, unto keeping unto the generations of the sons of Israel. For incorruptible and remaining always, and in every season and time most known is Christ. And he is opposite Lord—that is, in the eyes of the Father. For when the Only-begotten has come to be according to us, then also he has entered into the Holies of holies, through the greater and more perfect tent—that is, into the heaven, now to be manifested to the face of God for us, according as has been written. For he does not set himself in sight of the Father, but us as in himself, though having come to be from face and somehow as from eyes, through the transgression in Adam, and the sin that tyrannized over all. In Christ therefore we have had the approach, and the boldness unto the entrance of the Holies, just as wise Paul said to us. For just as also we have been raised together and seated together in the heavenly things in Christ, so again in him we have also come to be in face of the Father. And concerning the sacred jar let these things be said; and it signifies that Aaron’s rod also itself means Christ—come then let us say, if it seems good.
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: Korah then and indeed also Abiram, and in addition to this Dathan, sprouted from tribe and blood of Levi; and having been entrusted, he says, with a liturgy arranged by the votes from above in the holy tent, they have thirsted for the glory of Moses and of Aaron, snatching the honor for themselves, though not having been called toward this by God. And indeed also priding themselves unto harsh boldness, and being very supercilious, they were making the abuse against both no longer bearable, but altogether hard to carry; and as untamed bulls they were separating themselves, and shaking off the slavery under God, they were persuading other impious ones to leap away together with them. But they were exacting justice of the things dared by them. For the earth opening its mouth was sending down into Hades the boastful people, with those of the same race, tents and properties; and wishing to make clear that by the vote from above, and not by Moses’ wills, Aaron has been allotted the excelling order in priesthood, the lawgiver said toward all-excellent Moses: ‘Speak to the sons of Israel, and take from them a rod, according to houses of families, from all their rulers, according to houses of their families, twelve rods, and of each write his name upon the rod. And Aaron’s name write upon the rod of Levi. For there is one rod. According to tribe of house of their families they will
translator_notes: Ends mid δώσουσι into §13.

title: Aaron’s rod sprouts almonds; Emmanuel high priest; rod of Jesse blooms = resurrection
english: Cyril: …give. And you will set them in the tent of the testimony, opposite the testimony, in which I will be known to you there. And it will be, the human whom I should choose, his rod will sprout. And I will remove from me the murmuring of sons of Israel, which they themselves murmur upon you. And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all their rulers gave him a rod, to the one ruler a rod according to ruler, according to houses of their families, twelve rods. And Aaron’s rod in midst of their rods, and Moses set away the rods opposite Lord in the tent of the testimony. And it came to be on the morrow, and Moses and Aaron entered in the tent of the testimony. And behold Aaron’s rod sprouted unto house of Levi, and brought forth a sprout, and blossomed flowers, and sprouted almonds. And Moses brought out all the rods from face of Lord toward all sons of Israel. And they saw, and each took his rod. And Lord said toward Moses: Set away Aaron’s rod before the testimonies unto keeping, a sign for the sons of the disobedient. And let their murmuring cease from me, and they will not die.’ So then a sign not unclear of Aaron the divine having been taken out brightly and distinctly unto priest-work, as from Levi’s blood, is the blossoming of the rod. And when it is turned again unto spiritual contemplation, as still in thickest types, the mystery of Christ will shine up again.
Palladius: In what manner?

Cyril: For Emmanuel has been voted lawgiver together and high priest upon us by God and Father, bringing himself forward for us the sacrifice. For as blessed Paul said, ‘The law through Moses sets humans as high priests having weakness; but the word of the oath-taking after the law, a Son perfected unto the age.’ So then the Word has come down from heaven, and has come to be according to us, liturgist of the holy things and of the true tent which the Lord pitched, and not a human. But those from Israel’s blood did not seem to think upright things; and as setting out their own will against him they were striking in many ways with the arrows from envy, no longer sparing tongue, nor boldness, nor outlandish attempts, and destroying themselves the wretched ones, and finally they crucified. Yet the rod from Jesse’s root was blooming again; for Christ has grown up and lived again, having loosed the pangs of death, according as has been written; for being life according to nature, as God, how was it likely to be held by death, and not rather to wrestle down corruption? And just as the growing-up of the rod, and the unexpected sprouting-again of the already flowerless wood, was a sufficient sign for the more ancient ones that Aaron has been voted high priest through the vote from above; so we say that a bright and clear and very sufficient proof that Emmanuel is also God according to nature is the trampling of death, and living again in a God-fitting way. And indeed Christ himself, though
translator_notes: Ends mid into §14 Jonah sign.

title: Jonah sign = resurrection; almond rod = watchfulness; lamp oil and twelve loaves begin
english: Cyril: …being able to finish without toil and easily every one of the things beyond the likely and word, was saying to those asking the sign: ‘This generation is wicked; it asks a sign, and a sign will not be given it, except the sign of Jonah the prophet. For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea-monster three days and three nights, so will the Son of the human be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.’ So then a truly famous and conspicuous sign, and sufficient unto faith for those at least truly well-minded, that the Son is God according to nature and has been born from God Father, is the abolishing of death and corruption, and blooming again toward life. ‘For he himself has become firstfruit of those who have fallen asleep, and firstborn from the dead.’ And the sign has been given to the sons of the disobedient, that they might know that by vote of God and Father Christ has become high priest upon us, ‘holy, without-evil, undefiled, having been separated from the sinners, and having become higher than the heavens,’ according to what has been written.
Palladius: But Aaron’s rod has blossomed for us; for this just now the sacred word has shown us; and it blossomed almonds; and what then the riddle is, I am not able to think.

Cyril: Especially, O Palladius, nothing unlikely to suspect that the rod has been taken from an almond-tree. And it was in custom for the ancients to use also such scepters. And if indeed we must also fit a word fitting the contemplations, I would say again that which has somehow been noised about, and seems to some also acceptable as in faith, that the almond rod is not unable to produce sleeplessness, if it should lie toward someone’s head, perhaps somehow working the matter by natural powers according to God’s will. And the one knowing all things, and Craftsman of the wholes, will somehow also confirm us unto this saying toward Jeremiah: ‘What do you see, Jeremiah?’ And he saying ‘An almond staff’; and then toward this God: ‘You have seen uprightly,’ he says, ‘because I am awake upon my words, to do them.’ So then the almond rod would reasonably be thought a symbol of sleeplessness. And as a waking from sleep has come to be the living-again of Christ from dead ones. Therefore also through the Psalmist’s lyre he says: ‘I lay down and slept, I was raised, because Lord has taken hold of me.’
Palladius: True is the word.

Cyril: And concerning lamp and table, the one at least in the first tent, it has been written again thus: ‘And Lord spoke toward Moses saying: Charge the sons of Israel, and let them take pure oil, crushed unto light, to burn a lamp continually, outside the veil in the tent of the testimony; and Aaron and his sons will burn it from evening until morning before Lord continually, an age-long lawful thing unto your generations. Upon the pure lampstand you will burn the lamps opposite Lord until unto the morning. And you will take fine flour, and you will make it twelve
translator_notes: Ends mid twelve loaves into §15.

title: Pure oil = Church light; seven lamps Holies; one lamp first tent = lesser law light
english: Cyril: …loaves. Of two tenths will be the one loaf, and you will set them two settings, six loaves the one setting upon the pure table opposite Lord, and you will set upon the setting pure frankincense and salt, and they will be unto loaves unto remembrance set forth for the Lord. On the day of the sabbaths you will set forth opposite Lord continually before the sons of Israel, an age-long covenant; and it will be for Aaron and for his sons, and they will eat them in a holy place; for they are Holies of holies. This for him from the things sacrificed to the Lord, an age-long lawful thing.’ So then pure is the oil, and indeed also olive—that is, from olives, not from other-formed seeds and more earthy, from which oil was indeed pressed, but bastard as it were and somehow adulterated; for always pure and genuinely true in Churches is the light, clear that the one through Christ, by Spirit, even if it should be ministered through the voice of the saints, toward whom Christ said: ‘You are the light of the world.’ And nothing marvelous; for those whom he named brothers, and set as sharers of himself, to these he would reasonably also distribute the glory of his own dignities. So then the lamp is burned also in the first tent, and the matter would have a double mind; for in the more inward tent seven lamps shine, being kindled in the morning, and sending rich light to those running in. And the lampstand was Christ, as in type again illuminating with much and ample light those wishing to run into the Holies of holies; ‘For come toward him,’ he says, ‘and be illuminated.’ And indeed also the kindling of the lamps in the morning would signify the time of the becoming-human. For he has shone through, as some day, and intelligible light has shone up, driving the darkness of our ancient ignorance, and as in an order of night, scattering the mist that fell upon the hearts of all. For thus also the prophet was exhorting for us the time of the Savior’s sojourn saying: ‘In the morning you will hear my voice, in the morning I will stand beside you, and I will see.’ For when would the prayers of all have become acceptable, and we the formerly wandering have stood as it were beside God, through intimacy clearly spiritual, and hearing and faith, unless the light from heaven has shone upon us—that is, Christ? So then in the more inward tent rich and subtle is the light of the seven lamps, and in the first tent there was the lamp shining, showing, I think, that not apart from the divine light are even those themselves being pedagogued in law, the matter making clear. For also the law through Moses was calling from many-gods unto knowledge of the one by nature and truly God, and was removing the more ancient from still serving the creation beside the one who created, and was persuading that they must lie beside the Craftsman of all; and not apart from the intelligible light these things were being set upright in the souls of those pedagogued. So then, for I will say again, rich and much is the illumination from Christ for those unto the Holies of holies, and lesser for those in law; and true is the word
notes_covered: seven lamps vs one lamp = Gospel vs law light
translator_notes: Ends mid into §16 shadow not equal Gospel brightness.

title: Law shadow lesser; lamp = Baptist; twelve loaves = apostles around Christ
english: Cyril: …For in no way does the shadow in law weigh equal, unto spiritual brightness, with the Gospel oracles; for these flash around the whole inhabited world, and that was a mark for those from Israel alone.
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.
Cyril: And it seems, O Palladius, that the table and the lamp, the one at least in the first tent, also hint something else.
Palladius: What then do you say?
Cyril: Perhaps somehow the lamp is all-divine Baptist John, and the twelve breads pre-type for us the chorus of the holy apostles.
Palladius: In what manner?

Cyril: Or do you not know that for those in law and according to Judea the all-divine Baptist was as some lamp, going before Christ, and concerning him God and Father has announced beforehand: ‘I have prepared a lamp for my Christ.’ And the Savior himself has also witnessed this, saying to the leaders of the Jews concerning him. ‘That one was the lamp burning and shining, and you wished to rejoice for an hour in his light.’ For see how being law-learned blessed Paul all but brings back unto remembrance of a lamp, the one according to the first tent. For the lawgiver has ordered that it must be kept unquenched saying thus: ‘And Aaron and his sons will burn it from evening until morning before Lord continually.’ Yet having been pleased for a altogether brief time upon him, the Jews, through running toward the baptism through him, and catching much marvel upon him, put to sleep by death all but quenching the ever-shining lamp. For even if Herod’s daring should perhaps be said, yet being from Israel’s blood; on account of this Christ, accusing to the peoples of the Jews the boldness against every holy one, ‘It is not possible,’ he says, ‘for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.’
Palladius: So then light and lamp, according to likeness and according to participation of Christ, is also the all-divine Baptist for those in law according to Judea.

Cyril: Thus I say. And according to the equal manner we say the holy apostles are thought breads. For one is the bread by nature and truly, the one from heaven and life-making; and according to imitation of the one by nature and according to participation, breads nourishing unto piety are the divine mystagogues, putting into us words of life, and removing the famine from ignorance from the soul of those believing. And equal in number to the disciples are the breads; for twelve, and lying unto two settings, six from here, he says, and six from here, all but also standing around in a circle, and having lying in a middle place the one also from heaven—that is, Christ; and each of two tenths—that is, from two perfect measures. For the all-divine disciples have become perfect according to both, holding freshly toward every one of good things, conspicuous in deed and in word.
notes_covered: law shadow vs Gospel world light
translator_notes: §16 complete speaker cycle; frankincense/salt continue §17.

title: Frankincense/salt on loaves; sabbath = Christ-presence; types outside Holies
english: Cyril: Frankincense and salt are the things sprinkled upon them, the frankincense showing the fragrant in sanctification, and fragrance of Christ, and the salt at least hinting the prudence. For not without-understanding or foolish is the word of the saints, but seasoned in grace and salt, according to what has been written, and giving grace to those hearing. And it has also been said toward them by Christ: ‘You are the salt of the earth.’ And they are also set forth on a day of Sabbaths. For a day of showing-forth of the holy apostles is the time of the intelligible Sabbath—that is, the presence of Christ, which since those from Israel did not know, Paul says concerning them, ‘So then a sabbath-keeping is left for the people of God.’ For they did not enter into his rest, not having accepted the faith. So then an intelligible and true sabbath-keeping is the time of our Savior’s sojourn. And in God’s eyes is the setting-forth of the breads, and indeed also in Israel’s eyes. ‘For you will set forth,’ he says, ‘on the day of the Sabbaths opposite Lord through all, beside the sons of Israel’; of the one watching and continually deeming the saints worthy of oversight. ‘For eyes of Lord are upon righteous ones,’ he says. And of Israel, as owing to attend to them, and somehow as setting the eye of the mind upon, of which also the bodily would be unto a type. ‘But it will be,’ he says, ‘for Aaron and for his sons, and they will eat them.’ For the writings of the holy apostles are set forth for us unto food, for those justified in faith, a holy and sacred race, peoples unto acquisition, and chosen, and anointed with the grace of the holy Spirit.
Palladius: You have spoken well; for I would agree. But for what reason are the types of the holy Baptist, and of the holy apostles, not in the Holies of holies, but in the first tent?

Cyril: First because much is the intervening, and not in which Christ is will also the things of the saints lie, but somehow as outside and in lesser things. For the things of God have been taken out and are apart, and a long word walls off the human things, showing the property of the natures as incomparable, and the difference of the good-fame. Then because they have come to be from Jews and from the worship according to law. In this way then a place as fitting for them is the first tent, in which the altar of the fruit-offerings in types was lying; or did not the calling of the holy disciples come to be from Israel’s blood and as from the first tent?
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: So then with the word concerning these holding sufficiently for us very well, one must bring alongside, if it seems good, the voice of all-divine Paul, clarifying gracefully the witness upon at least the first and the second tent. And he writes thus: ‘And these things having been constructed thus
notes_covered: Col 4:6 salt/grace; Matt 5:13 salt of earth
Baptist/apostles types in first tent not Holies
translator_notes: Ends mid Paul quote into §18.

title: Heb 9: priests always / high priest once; Christ own blood; one offering forever
english: Cyril: …into the first tent, through all the priests enter performing the worships. And into the second, once of the year alone the high priest not apart from blood, which he brings forward for himself and for the ignorances of the people, this of the holy Spirit making clear that the way of the holies has not yet been manifested, while the first tent still has standing. Which is a parable unto the time that has stood in, according to which gifts and sacrifices are brought forward, not able according to conscience to perfect the one worshipping, only upon foods and drinks and differing baptisms righteous-ordinances of flesh laid on until a time of setting-upright. But Christ having arrived high priest of the coming good things through the greater and more perfect tent not hand-made—that is, not of this creation—nor through blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood has entered once-for-all into Holies of holies having found age-long ransom.’ So then you understand that the priests were performing the worships in the first tent, not having the running-in unto Holies of holies. For somehow such is the worship according to law, having standing in shadows. And these are empty toward cleansing and washing-off of sin. For you have just learned Paul crying that they have insufficiently according to conscience to perfect the one worshipping. And it was rather being kept until a time of setting-upright, clear that of the becoming-human of the Only-begotten, when the unbeauty of the types has withdrawn unto truth. ‘And once of the year and alone the high priest was running into the Holies of holies. And not apart from blood, which he was bringing forward for both himself and for the ignorances of the people.’ And all-wise Paul will also clarify this again for us saying thus concerning Christ, ‘Saying above, that sacrifices and offerings and whole-burnt-offerings and concerning sin you did not will, nor were well-pleased, which are brought forward according to law. Then I said, Behold I have come to do your will’; he takes away the first that he may set the second; ‘In which will we have been sanctified, through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ; and every high priest stands according to day liturgizing, and bringing forward the same sacrifices many times which are never able to take away sins, having brought forward no sacrifice for sins, unto the continual he has sat at the right of God; the rest awaiting until his enemies be set a footstool of his feet, for by one offering he has perfected unto the continual those being sanctified.’ For having died once, he no longer dies, according to what has been written; and having borne up sins of many, he has entered into the Holies of holies—that is, into the heaven, now to be manifested to the face of God for us.

Palladius: Clear is the word; so then release the sweat upon this, and what blood again would it be which it is custom for the leader of the sacred things to bring forward for both himself and for the ignorances of the people, speak to me asking.
translator_notes: Paul block continues from §17; blood question opens §19.

title: Lev 4 anointed priest’s calf; blood into Holies; Christ cleanses priest and people
english: Cyril: Being law-learned Paul and having exacted most of all the command through Moses, as to peoples of the Hebrews wise in such things, and having read the law, concerning the things thus solemn and very ineffable, not in breadth of narrations, but rather in passing-by and reminder of the things already known beforehand, he addresses such things. And I will bring alongside, if it seems good, also the law upon this for one having chosen to learn well, and having thirsted very well for the exact and very polished unto clarifying of the contemplations. So then it has been written in the Leviticus: ‘And Lord spoke toward Moses saying: Speak toward the sons of Israel; A soul, if it should sin opposite Lord unwillingly from all the commands of Lord, which one must not do, and should do one something from them, if the anointed high priest should sin, unto the people sinning, he will bring forward concerning his sin which he sinned, a calf from cattle unblemished to the Lord concerning the sin, and he will bring forward the calf beside the door of the tent of the testimony opposite Lord, and he will slaughter the calf before Lord. And the anointed priest having been perfected taking the hands from the blood of the calf, will bring it into the tent of the testimony, and the priest will dip the finger into the blood, and will sprinkle from the blood seven times opposite Lord, according to the holy veil. And the priest will set from the blood of the calf upon the horns of the altar of the incense of the composition opposite Lord, which is in the tent of the testimony, and all the blood of the calf he will pour out beside the base of the altar of the whole-burnt-offerings, which is beside the doors of the tent of the testimony, and all the fat of the calf of the sin he will remove from it… and they will bring out the whole calf outside the camp unto a clean place, where they pour out the ash. And they will burn it upon woods in fire; upon the pouring-out of the ash it will be burned.’ These things the law has ordered to come to be, if something of the failings from ignorance should be registered of the one excelling in priesthood. And he says that also for the ignorances of the people a sacrifice of a calf must be finished being brought and slaughtered thus beside the doors of the tent of the testimony opposite Lord, and with the elders of the Synagogue having set their hands upon it, and with the blood being brought into the Holies of holies, and to say simply all things being finished upon it according to likeness of the sacrifice for Aaron. But that Christ is cleansing both of priests and of people—for we have been justified in him the from the sin
translator_notes: Ends mid ἀποτριβόμενοι into §20; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Unblemished calf = Christ; hands = deeds; sevenfold blood = perfect cleansing
english: Cyril: …being rubbed-off pollution, and through these also it would become clear for everyone. And let us say part by part the things upon each of the things written; for the word would go forward distinctly and unfolding, as possible, the things hidden.
Palladius: You have spoken well.

Cyril: So then the calf is taken unblemished and unwounded unto a type of Christ the truly unblemished, and not having endured to suffer the wounding from the sin. ‘For the ruler of this world comes,’ he says, ‘and in me he will find nothing’; for he did not do sin, according to the Scriptures. And he is brought forward toward the very doors of the holy tent opposite Lord, as not refusing the suffering, for the holy tent—that is, the Church—having been dedicated for it unto a smell of fragrance to God and Father. Therefore also he was saying, ‘For them I sanctify myself.’ Saying the, I sanctify, instead of, I bring forward, and dedicate an unblemished offering to God and Father. For what is dedicated to God is said to be sanctified, according to that somehow written: ‘A snare for a man, to sanctify something of his own quickly; for after vowing, repenting comes to be.’ And that the offering is acceptable and well-pleasing, the, ‘Opposite Lord,’ makes clear. For we already think what has been written upon the pair of brothers, Cain I mean and Abel. ‘For God looked,’ he says, ‘upon Abel and upon his gifts, and upon Cain and his sacrifices he did not attend’; for he looks upon what is pleasing to him, and turns away hating what does not hold thus, not unclearly. And with the hands of the one who has failed being set upon the calf, the slaughter is practiced; and before Lord. ‘For he himself takes up our sins, and for us is pained’ being slaughtered. For of deed and practices is the hand, unto a type. Yet, before Lord he is slaughtered, all but with the Father also coming-down unto the needing for the Son to have died for us; for he does not turn away seeing him slaughtered, and not somehow altogether praising the suffering, yet not having been ignorant that it is saving for the world for Emmanuel to suffer for us. So then he himself takes up our sins, and for us is pained, enduring for us the slaughter upon the honored cross. Then the priest taking from the blood with the finger, will sprinkle seven times upon the holy veil, which was upon the ark. And its name, the mercy-seat. And he also anoints the horns of the altar of the incense. For Christ has become for us both propitiation and mercy-seat. Yet, in blood of an age-long covenant, he gifts us the most complete cleansing-off. For this, I think, is the mercy-seat being sprinkled with the blood seven times; and a symbol of perfection is the number seven. For his death also makes fragrant the salvation and life of the world and the approach in faith; ‘For one died for all, that those living may no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died for them and was raised,’ according to the Scriptures. So then the anointing of the golden censer with the blood makes clear the fragrance of the death. And the remaining blood is also poured out beside the base of the altar of the fruit-
translator_notes: Ends mid καρπωμάτων into §21; PG mid-cut kept.
